title: Reactions now notify the person you reacted to
summary: Emoji reactions now send a notification to the author of the message you reacted to — a thumbs up reads as a real acknowledgement, so it should reach the person it's meant for. The notification shows the actual emoji next to the label in the bell, in browser push, and in the Slack DM for task comments. Only the message author is notified, never yourself, and only when a reaction is added — taking one back is silent. Repeat reacting is collapsed: if the same person reacts again on the same task or person within an hour, it stays a single notification rather than a burst.

title: Emoji reactions on people updates and task comments
summary: You can now react to a message with an emoji instead of writing a reply — on the People page Updates log and on task board comments. Hover a message and click the smiley to pick from a fixed set (👍 🎉 ❤️ 😂 👀 🙌 🔥 ✅); click an existing reaction pill to add yours or take it back. Each pill shows a count and names who reacted on hover, and highlights when you are one of them. Reactions are stored per user so two people reacting at the same time can't overwrite each other, and they are removed automatically when the message is deleted. Reactions deliberately send no notification — they are the quiet alternative to a reply. Also fixed a long-standing bug where editing a People update didn't visibly update the entry until the page was reloaded.

title: Video playback: quality controls now activate in Chrome/Edge
summary: Fixed the reason the new video quality controls weren't appearing in Chromium browsers. Edge (and Chrome/Firefox) falsely report that they can play HLS natively, so the player was handing video straight to the browser's built-in player and never loading the advanced player (hls.js) — which meant no quality button and no start-quality tuning. The player now uses hls.js whenever the browser supports it and only falls back to native playback on iOS Safari, so the Auto/HD quality toggle and faster high-quality start now actually take effect. The Cloudflare bandwidth hint from the previous change was confirmed working. Note: because hls.js fetches the manifest with a CORS check, the LPOS domain must be in each Cloudflare video's allowed origins (the tailnet host already is).

title: Video playback: open at high quality via Cloudflare bandwidth hint
summary: Videos that opened blurry and took a few seconds to sharpen should now open at high quality across all browsers, including Safari and Edge. The fix is applied at the source: the stream route appends Cloudflare's clientBandwidthHint to the video manifest, telling Cloudflare to start at a high rendition instead of the lowest — so it doesn't depend on any in-browser player tuning (which had missed Safari entirely and wasn't visibly helping Edge). The hint is only added to Cloudflare manifests, never to Frame.io URLs, so pre-signed links aren't broken. Also removed the unintuitive rewind behavior that only reached full resolution after fast-forwarding first, and added temporary diagnostics to pin down why the manual quality button wasn't appearing in Chromium browsers.

title: Platform passes: generate tile hero images (pipework, placeholder-backed)
summary: The Platform pass studio can now generate a hero image for a tile from its title and description, not just accept an uploaded one. The tile inspector's image control is now Generate / Upload / Use video frame, with an editable prompt override and a Regenerate button; the auto-built prompt uses a house style guide (docs/platform-image-style.md) so every image aims for the same cinematic, tonally-consistent look, and the result is duotoned onto the pass's brand exactly like an uploaded photo. The whole pipeline is wired end-to-end but the actual image API is intentionally not connected yet — generation currently returns a single tonal placeholder so the flow can be seen working; going live is a small, isolated change (implement the OpenAI gpt-image-1 seam and add the key). Also corrected the tile design/export dimensions to the real 300x400 (3:4) aspect.

title: Faster full-quality video start + viewer quality toggle
summary: Videos used to open blurry and take 4-5 seconds to climb to full quality — that's HLS adaptive bitrate starting low and ramping up, and the player was left completely untuned. The player now starts with an optimistic bandwidth estimate (5 Mbps) so it opens at a high rendition on fast connections and only steps down if the connection genuinely can't keep up, which shrinks the visible ramp for everyone. Two new controls give deterministic full resolution: an Auto⇄HD button in the player (Chrome/Firefox HLS sources) that pins the top quality, and an automatic fast-path that serves full resolution immediately when you scrub back toward the start after quality has already been proven sustainable. Safari and older MP4 sources are unaffected (no button shown).

title: Hiring report: export candidate Q&A as Markdown
summary: A candidate's hiring report now has "Copy Q&A" and "Download .md" buttons at the top, next to their name. Both produce a single clean Markdown document listing every question and the candidate's answer, in section order, with none of the on-screen scoring/timing clutter and no tiny text — built for pasting or uploading into an AI to ask follow-up questions about the responses. It's a client-side export (no PDF, no new dependency): multiple-choice answers show the chosen option text, written answers show the field text, and repeated-item answers list each item. Scoring is intentionally excluded.

title: Cloudflare storage budget cap corrected to 4000 minutes
summary: The Cloudflare library panel in admin showed usage against a 3000-minute cap, but that number was a hardcoded UI constant that didn't match the actual Stream plan of 4000 minutes. Bumped the constant to 4000 so the "X / 4000 min used" counter and its progress bar reflect the real plan size. The used-minutes figure was already accurate (summed from live Cloudflare video durations); only the total/cap was wrong. Note this cap is still a static constant, not read live from Cloudflare, so it needs a manual edit if the plan changes again.

title: Removed the Review check-in banner from task details
summary: The gold "While this edit sits in Review, LPOS re-pings every 3 days…" banner (and its Acknowledge button) no longer appears in the task detail modal — it was redundant clutter. The behind-the-scenes 3-day check-in itself is unchanged: assignees still get the periodic bell/Slack/push nudge for edits sitting in Review, and posting an update still resets the clock.

title: Clearer Cloudflare 'out of storage' upload errors
summary: When a video fails to upload because your Cloudflare Stream plan is out of storage, LPOS now shows a plain-English explanation — telling you the account has hit its storage limit and to delete unused videos or buy more storage minutes — instead of the raw Cloudflare error like "Storage capacity exceeded (code 10011)". This covers the storage-limit case wherever it appears during the upload, and the original Cloudflare text is still available via the "Show full error" toggle for debugging.

title: Daily Catch-Up groups activity by client
summary: The Daily Catch-Up now describes where activity is happening by CLIENT name rather than individual project name — both in the recap headline and on each item row. So instead of "CFA - Jeremy Pollack" you'll see "Chick-fil-A," and activity spread across several projects for the same client is rolled up under that one client. It intentionally doesn't drill down to which specific project within a client, since client names are the more recognizable unit day to day.

title: Daily Catch-Up highlights which projects are active
summary: The Daily Catch-Up recap now leads with WHERE the activity is happening — naming the specific project(s) behind each category and how much of it landed in each (e.g. "13 uploads across three projects led by CFA - Jeremy Pollack (9 of 13)… media activity concentrated in July Town Hall (13 of 30)"). Project context is now central to the morning headline rather than just raw counts, and when activity spans several projects it names the top ones instead of implying it was all one.

title: Daily Catch-Up uses first names
summary: The Daily Catch-Up now refers to people by first name only (e.g. "Jordan" instead of "Jordan Johnson") — in the recap headline, the per-item rows, and the contributor breakdown — for a friendlier, less formal morning update.

title: Daily Catch-Up headline: accurate credit for who did what
summary: Follow-up to the personal Daily Catch-Up: tightened the AI morning headline so it credits each person with their own share of the work rather than the whole category. Previously it could say someone "drove 13 uploads" when they did only 3 of them (the rest being automated Frame.io/ingest activity with no person attached). The recap now says e.g. "uploaded, led by KC Cohen with 3 of them" and "7 task updates driven primarily by Jordan Johnson with 5 of them." Note: task activity carries reliable names; some uploads are system/ingest with no person; and video-asset comments currently have no stored author, so "who commented" can't be shown until Frame.io comment sync captures the commenter.

title: Daily Catch-Up now names who did what
summary: The Daily Catch-Up recap is more personal — instead of only counting activity by type, it now credits the people behind the work. Each item in the drawer shows who did it (the uploader, the person who left a comment, the note author), and the AI morning headline now names the people driving each category (e.g. who drove uploads or left key comments) rather than just reporting numbers. Automated/system activity stays anonymous since there's no person to credit. Past days already summarized before this change will start showing names once rebuilt.

title: Lighting picks up lights that come online mid-session
summary: Fixed a Lighting issue where a fixture that was powered on (or Bluetooth-reconnected) after LPOS had already connected to Amaran Desktop stayed invisible in LPOS even though the Amaran app showed it connected. LPOS only re-scanned for new fixtures on connect or when you hit Refresh; its 30-second background poll just updated lights it already knew about. The poll now also re-scans the fixture list every cycle, so a light that joins mid-session shows up on its own within about 30 seconds — no more hitting Refresh to make a missing Void/Bookshelf/Mobile light appear. Lights that briefly drop off are still kept on screen so a momentary blip doesn't remove a tile mid-shoot.

title: Clearer, safer "Approve all" for cold-storage cleanup
summary: The "Approve all" button in Raw Footage Cold Storage no longer looks frozen while it works. Deleting a large batch from Backblaze now runs in the background with live "Purging N of M" progress and a shrinking review list, so you can even leave the page. Clicking again while a run is in progress no longer starts a second overlapping deletion — the button is guarded — and per-file Approve/Spare are paused until the batch finishes. No change to what actually gets deleted; the delete logic was already correct, this just makes the progress visible and prevents duplicate runs.

title: Fix crash when a streaming page is closed early
summary: Fixed a recurring server crash ("ReadableStream is already closed") that could take down the app when someone navigated away from, or lost connection to, a page that streams live data — slate playback downloads, Cami chat, poster images, and Sony camera live-view. These streams now stop cleanly the moment the viewer disconnects instead of trying to keep sending data to a closed connection.

title: 3-day check-in for tasks sitting in Review
summary: Editing tasks that sit in the In Review status now get a gentle 3-day check-in, modelled on the handoff nudge. LPOS re-pings the task assignees (in-app bell, Slack, and web push) every 3 days while a task waits in Review. Posting an update or clicking the new Acknowledge button in the task resets the 3-day clock; moving the task out of Review ends the check-in, and reassigning it via Handoff lets the handoff nudge take over instead. The threshold and sweep cadence are admin-tunable (default 3 days / 15 min).

title: Right-click Copy Path on project tabs
summary: You can now right-click any tab inside a project (Media, Photos, Scripts, Transcripts, Assets, Pass Prep, Client Uploads) and choose Copy Path to get a shareable deep link straight to that tab. Paste the link to a teammate and it opens the project on the exact tab. To make this work the active tab is now reflected in the URL as a ?tab= parameter, so links copied from the address bar deep-link too.

title: Architecture analysis: public-web split & studio bridge
summary: Planning/analysis only — no product change. Mapped what it would take to run parts of LPOS on the public web while keeping hardware and local processes on the studio PC behind a bridge. Concluded LPOS is currently one process on the studio machine with Tailscale as its de-facto security perimeter, proposed a three-tier split (public/cloud, internal-portable, studio-bound), and recommended promoting the existing editpanel token+heartbeat pattern into a first-class outbound studio agent rather than exposing the studio via an inbound tunnel.

title: Cleaner camera logs
summary: Camera connection messages no longer flood or garble the log. A camera that keeps failing to connect now reports it once instead of repeating every 15 seconds, retry attempts aren't spelled out line by line, and messages from different cameras no longer scramble together — each line stays intact and readable.

title: Sync timecode across the studio cameras
summary: A new Sync timecode button in the camera settings sets all armed Sony cameras to the same time-of-day timecode (Free-Run) from LPOS's clock. Run it between takes to keep your multicam clips aligned and easy to stack in the edit. It's a software sync — accurate to the network, not frame-locked like a hardware jam — and it's manual on purpose, so it never changes timecode in the middle of a recording.

title: FX3 starts recording in sync with the FX6s
summary: The FX3 uses a different record command, and the system was discovering that by trying the FX6 command first and falling back — which made the FX3 start recording a beat behind the other cameras. It now knows from the camera model to use the FX3's command straight away, so all cameras roll together on the REC button.

title: Camera battery percentage is now accurate
summary: Camera battery was being read from a coarse level indicator and shown as a nonsense percentage — a camera at ~66% displayed as 4%. It now reads the camera's actual battery percentage. This corrects the reading on both FX3 and FX6 bodies.

title: FX3 record support
summary: The FX3 uses a different record command than the FX6 and was rejecting the studio's record button. The camera bridge now recognizes this and uses the right command for each camera automatically — trying one, falling back to the other, and remembering which each body accepts. So the REC button can drive FX3 and FX6 bodies side by side.

title: Studio wording and lighting layout polish
summary: Clearer captions on the camera settings (what the Camera control switch and Sony cameras section do), and the lighting tab's top controls now sit tight under the header with All lights on the left and the status, settings, and Presets grouped on the right.

title: FX3 cameras now show status, not just connect
summary: An FX3 would connect but show no status — battery, recording state, and the rest stayed blank. The cause: the studio decided whether a camera was reachable by checking a single network port that the FX3 doesn't use, so it was treated as offline despite a working connection. Reachability now checks the ports these cameras actually answer on (including the one the FX3 uses), so FX3 bodies report status like the FX6s. A one-time power-cycle may be needed if an FX3 is still holding an old session.

title: A camera that can't confirm it stopped is now flagged, not left rolling
summary: If the system briefly lost solid contact with a camera at the moment you pressed stop, it could wrongly assume the camera was already stopped and skip the stop entirely — leaving that camera recording while everything looked fine. Stopping now refuses to assume: if it can't actually read whether the camera is recording, it reconnects and, failing that, reports the camera as not-confirmed-stopped so you know to check it, rather than silently leaving it rolling.

title: Multi-camera control fix now actually reaches the cameras
summary: The recent fix that gives each camera its own hardware address to the Sony SDK wasn't taking effect on the status/monitoring path: the address was being scrambled in transit, so the system kept treating all cameras as one and they fought over a single connection. That transit bug is fixed, so the per-camera addressing now applies everywhere. A camera still stuck holding an old connection from before may need one power-cycle to clear.

title: Turn the whole camera tier off — and it idles itself when cameras are away
summary: The Cameras tab has a new Camera control switch that stops the Sony bridge entirely when you flip it off — no connection attempts, monitoring, or record fan-out. Even left on, the system now idles itself: after all cameras have been off the network for 10 minutes it stops hammering and quietly waits, then reconnects on its own the moment a camera powers back on. If cameras stay dark for 2 hours, admins get a one-time Slack heads-up. None of this can strand a shoot — a camera you turn on is picked up within seconds.

title: Cleaner, more consistent studio tabs
summary: The studio tabs now share one header style — same size and placement across ATEM, Lighting, Camera, Audio, and Playback. The ATEM tab loses the large program/preview boxes (the live/cued camera still shows on the angle buttons, which are now more square), and the lighting controls collapse onto a single line: status and presets on the left, all-lights on the right, with Refresh and Disconnect tucked into a settings dialog that matches the ATEM one.

title: Multiple Sony cameras can finally be controlled at the same time
summary: Only one camera could ever hold a connection: the studio was telling the Sony SDK that every camera had the same hardware address, so all of them looked like a single device. Connecting one would knock the others offline, and control would rotate unpredictably between them. Each camera's real hardware address, already captured during the network scan, is now used — so all armed cameras can connect and record together. Cameras added by hand rather than by scanning have no hardware address on file; re-run the network scan for those.

title: Cameras no longer fail to connect on startup with a misleading credentials error
summary: Right after LPOS starts, a camera's security handshake can briefly fail while the camera is still waking up. The studio would give up on that first attempt and then report what looked like a wrong username or password. It now retries the handshake a few times, and if it genuinely cannot complete it, says so plainly instead of blaming the credentials.

title: A busy camera now points at the right cause
summary: When a camera reports that it is already in use, the message now says what is actually true most of the time: a previous camera bridge process on this machine exited without letting go of the camera. It will time out on its own, or you can power-cycle the camera to clear it immediately. Other apps connecting to the camera are still mentioned, but no longer listed first — that was sending people to check their phones instead of the studio Mac.

title: A camera that never started recording no longer reports a failed stop
summary: If a camera refused to start recording, pressing stop afterwards would report that the camera failed to stop — implying it might still be rolling, when it had never started. The studio now decides whether a camera is rolling by asking the camera, rather than by whether the last command succeeded. A stop sent to a camera that is not recording is treated as nothing to do. Cameras whose state cannot be read are still flagged as possibly rolling after a stop, since that is the safer assumption. Separately, when a camera refuses to record, the error now suggests checking for a memory card — the most common cause.

title: Fixed a camera getting permanently stuck as 'already connected'
summary: A camera could get wedged in a state where every reconnection attempt was rejected because the camera SDK was silently holding its own background connection — one the studio software could neither see nor close, and which survived every attempt to reset the connection. The bridge now disables the SDK's background reconnection entirely and manages reconnection itself, which it was already doing. A camera stuck in this state before the fix needs one power-cycle to clear it.

title: Cameras recover on their own when their connection goes stale
summary: If a camera's control session quietly dies, the studio would keep talking to the dead connection and every record, stop, and status check would fail until the bridge was restarted. The bridge now recognizes a dead session, rebuilds the connection, and retries once — so a stale connection heals itself instead of taking the camera out for the rest of the shoot. Genuine refusals from the camera are still reported.

title: Camera connection errors now say what actually went wrong
summary: When a Sony camera fails to connect, the log now explains the reason in plain language instead of always blaming the camera's username and password. The most common cause is that another app or a leftover session is already controlling the camera — an FX6 only allows one remote connection at a time. Also fixed a bug where a single failed connection attempt would poison every retry afterwards with a misleading follow-up error, hiding the original reason the camera refused.

title: ATEM settings is now a centered dialog with Travel, File, and Cameras tabs
summary: The ATEM settings menu opens as a centered dialog instead of sliding up and sticking to the bottom of the screen, and its contents are split across three tabs: Travel (travel mode, setup checklist, pause reconnect, and the ATEM connection), File (record filename), and Cameras (the Sony camera roster). The per-camera password boxes have been removed from the roster rows, since every camera in the studio shares one login. Connection errors still show no matter which tab you are on.

title: Each studio camera can now have its own password
summary: Cameras in the studio roster can each store their own Access Authentication user and password, instead of every camera being forced to share a single set. Previously, a camera whose password differed from the first one would silently fail to start or stop recording while still showing as online — because the online indicator only checks that the camera answers on the network, not that we can actually control it. That indicator now turns amber when a camera is reachable but the control session fails, the camera bridge reports the real error instead of discarding it, and every start/stop attempt is logged per camera.

title: Batch download project assets as a zip
summary: You can now select multiple files (and folders) in a project's Assets tab and download them all at once as a single .zip. Selected folders keep their structure inside the archive, and picking just one file downloads it directly as before. Works for both locally-stored and Google Drive-backed assets.

title: Publishing to Cloudflare now reliably removes the old copy
summary: Closed the source of stale Cloudflare copies: when a new version of a video is published, the system now reliably deletes the immediately-previous live copy instead of occasionally picking the wrong record and leaving old copies behind. This was the underlying reason a video could accumulate several copies in Cloudflare. Existing leftover copies are still cleaned up by the nightly orphan detector (flag for manual purge) and by force reset.

title: Fix Firefox video playback across the library
summary: Fixed videos failing to play in Firefox inside LPOS. Firefox loads video differently than Chrome/Safari and is stricter about cross-origin permissions, so 214 older videos (about 40% of the library, all uploaded before 2026-06-28) were being blocked because they only permitted playback on the LeaderPass platform domain, not the internal LPOS address. Updated all 214 on Cloudflare to also permit the LPOS tailnet host — additive, so their existing LeaderPass protection is unchanged. New uploads since 2026-06-28 already include both and were unaffected. Hard-refresh Firefox to clear the previously-failed load.

title: Fix videos wrongly showing as "stale" after multiple re-pushes
summary: Fixed a bug where a video could show as out-of-date ("stale") in LPOS even when its current version was live on Cloudflare — and where LPOS could point at an old, already-deleted Cloudflare copy. It happened when an earlier version of a video had been pushed to Cloudflare more times than the current version: the internal ranking compared per-version attempt counts across versions, so the older version could win. LPOS now always picks the newest version's most recent Cloudflare publication. This corrected 24 active videos that were mis-labeled, and is what made the reported video keep looking stale/stuck after a force reset.

title: Force reset now clears old Cloudflare copies of a video
summary: Force-resetting a video no longer leaves its old Cloudflare copies piling up in the account. The reset now finds every Cloudflare copy of that video, keeps only the most recent one that is actually live and playable, and deletes the rest — then points LPOS at the surviving copy so the embed keeps working. As a safety guard, if none of the copies is confirmed live yet (for example a stuck upload with no earlier good version), it deletes nothing and falls back to the old behavior of clearing the state so you can re-push.

title: Edit button on your new comments appears instantly
summary: Fixed a brief delay where the Edit button on a comment you just posted only showed up about a second after posting. The comment-post response now reports the author-edit flag directly (the poster is always the author), so the Edit affordance is present the moment the comment appears — in both the sidebar and theater comment views — instead of waiting for the next background refresh to fill it in.

title: Edit media comments from theater mode too
summary: The full-screen theater player's comment panel now has the same edit button the sidebar comment list already had. Hovering your own comment shows a pencil icon that swaps the comment into an inline editor (⌘↵ to save, Esc to cancel); edits save immediately and stay in sync between the theater and sidebar views. Only your own top-level comments are editable, matching the sidebar.

title: Task comments can now be edited
summary: You can now edit a task comment after posting it, not just delete it. Hovering your own comment in a task's Updates thread reveals an Edit button that swaps the comment into an inline editor (with @mention support); Save updates the text and the comment shows a subtle '(edited)' marker. Only the original author can edit, and only plain comments — handoff and acknowledgement entries stay locked as system records. Matches the edit behavior media comments already had.

title: Move between projects now handles same-name collisions
summary: Moving an asset into a project that already has one with the same name no longer silently creates a duplicate. Before the move commits, a preflight checks the target for name collisions; if any exist, the move dialog asks — per asset — whether the moved file is a new version of the existing one (it's stacked on as the next version), a keep-both (renamed with a " (1)" suffix), or a skip (left in the source project, which is the default when the file is an exact byte-for-byte duplicate already present). Assets with no name clash move exactly as before. Merging re-parents the moved asset's versions onto the existing asset and removes the now-empty original.

title: LeaderPass AI: turbo-quality transcripts on provision + secret rename
summary: Videos sent to LeaderPass AI now carry a high-quality large-v3-turbo word-level transcript instead of the fast 'base' one. Normal LPOS ingest is unchanged and still uses base (snappy) — the turbo transcript is produced only at provision time, cached per video so re-provisioning doesn't redo the work, and never disturbs the transcript shown in the Transcripts tab. Because turbo transcription takes real time, provisioning a project (toggle-on, Re-provision, or a video finishing publish) is now a background 'transcribe-then-push' batch: each video is pushed the moment its own turbo transcript finishes. Also renamed the ingest credential to LPAI_PROVISIONING_SECRET to match the LeaderPass AI side (which now reads PROVISIONING_SECRET) — LPAI_BASE_URL is unchanged.

title: Verified: Drive folder backfill is non-destructive
summary: Confirmed via a full call-path trace that the Settings → Drive 'Check / Create All Project Folders' backfill cannot delete any content. It only finds-or-creates missing folders (idempotent — existing folders are reused untouched). The only non-additive action is in the orphaned-folder adoption branch, which moves (never deletes) loose files into a project's Assets folder, and only runs when a tracked orphan record matches. The destructive delete/trash helpers are never called on this path. Safe to run against live Drive data.

title: Promoted clients now get Drive folders + one-time backfill audit
summary: Fixed the gap where projects auto-created by promoting a prospect never got their Google Drive folder tree (so the Assets tab had nothing to resolve to). Extracted the folder-provisioning logic into a single shared setupProjectDriveFolders helper and now call it from every project-creation path: direct create, and both branches of prospect promotion (fold-into-existing-client and new-standalone-client). Centralising it prevents this drift from recurring. Also upgraded the admin one-time check: Settings → Drive → 'Check / Create All Project Folders' now runs an idempotent audit across every project and reports how many were newly created vs already set up vs failed, listing each newly-created project — so you can confirm all current clients have proper folders and repair any that were missing. Requires a server restart to take effect; the button repairs existing data on click.

title: Analysis: promoted clients/projects skip Assets-tab drive sync
summary: Investigation (no code changed). Confirmed that projects auto-created via prospect promotion do NOT get the Google Drive folder tree that direct project creation sets up. Direct creation (POST /api/projects) calls setupProjectDriveFolders after create(), building the LPOS/{client}/{project}/{Scripts,Transcripts,Assets,Workbooks} tree and caching folder IDs. The promotion route (POST /api/prospects/[id]/promote) auto-creates a project via the same store.create() in both branches but never calls setupProjectDriveFolders, so no folders are created or cached. Because folders are resolved at runtime from the clientName+projectName cache (not stored on the project row), a promoted project's Assets tab has nothing to resolve — promoteToDrive() then throws 'Drive folders not set up for this project'. Suggested fix: call setupProjectDriveFolders in both promotion branches, or move it into the shared store create()/post-create hook so all creation paths stay in sync. Already-promoted projects would need a backfill.

title: Transcription quality upgrade: selectable whisper model + word-level timecodes
summary: Transcription accuracy is now tunable from admin Settings without a redeploy. A new Transcription (Whisper) card lets you pick the whisper.cpp model — base (fast, the safe default), large-v3-turbo (recommended: near large-v3 accuracy, much faster), or large-v3 (highest accuracy) — and set worker count and per-job timeout, including a 'scale timeout with video length' option so long videos no longer trip the old fixed 15-minute cap. The card warns when a chosen model file isn't installed and when big models are run with more than one worker (they contend for the single GPU). Under the hood, every transcription now also writes an additive word-level timing sidecar (one entry per word with millisecond offsets) alongside the existing txt/srt/vtt/json outputs, feeding downstream products that need word-accurate timecodes; the existing Transcripts UI is completely unaffected. Requires the large model file to be downloaded onto the host before selecting it.

title: LeaderPass AI provisioning: per-project "Use in LeaderPass AI" toggle
summary: Projects now have a "Use in LeaderPass AI" toggle in their header. Turning it on pushes that project's Cloudflare-published videos to LeaderPass AI's ingest endpoint (one request per video: pass name, Cloudflare UID, title, and the transcript mapped to millisecond {startMs,endMs,text} cues). Transcripts prefer the word-level file when present and fall back to the whisper segment JSON. There's a manual Re-provision button that reports pushed/skipped/failed counts, and new videos auto-provision when they finish publishing to Cloudflare (the moment they first have a Cloudflare UID). The whole feature stays dormant until the LPAI_BASE_URL and LPAI_PROVISIONING_SECRET credentials are set in Doppler, per-video failures never abort the batch, and every push is logged to the activity timeline. Turning the toggle off just stops future pushes.

title: Studio lighting: master All On/Off toggle next to Presets
summary: Added a little All On/Off switch beside the Presets button on the studio lighting page. Flipping it turns every paired fixture on or off in one tap — it loops the existing per-fixture power command across all lights, so the individual ON/OFF buttons and live status stay in sync. The switch sits 'on' (green) only when every fixture is on, shows 'Working…' while a bulk run is in flight, and is disabled when lighting is disconnected or no fixtures are present.

title: Cold storage deletes now reclaim space + live Backblaze footprint check
summary: Made the Raw Footage Cold Storage admin self-sufficient so you never need to open Backblaze. Deletes (per-object, approve-all, and folder delete in the bucket browser) now permanently purge every version of a file via ListObjectVersions + batched DeleteObjects, reclaiming the space immediately — previously a delete only wrote a hide-marker on the versioned bucket and the data kept billing, which is why LPOS's tracked total read far smaller than Backblaze's. Added a 'Live Backblaze footprint' panel with a 'Check live footprint' button that walks every version in the bucket and shows current vs old/hidden versions vs total billed bytes next to LPOS's tracked total, so tracked-vs-actual is visible in-app. The accidental-delete safety flow (a file must be missing from source for the full retention window, then an admin must explicitly Approve or Spare) is unchanged.

title: Frame.io comment decoupling Step 5 (cleanup) — route rename + dead-code removal
summary: Cleanup after the decoupling. Renamed the comments API route off its Frame.io-branded path (app/api/projects/[projectId]/media/[assetId]/frameio/comments → .../comments) via git mv, since it now reads the local media_comments table; updated the 9 client fetch URLs (6 in MediaDetailPanel, 3 in MediaPlayer) plus the moved route's docstring/log tags. Removed the dead FrameIOInfo.commentCount field and its default (retired in Step 4, computed-on-read replaced it; the canonical projection spreads defaultFrameIO so nothing else referenced it). Spawned a separate sub-task to fix the editpanel Resolve-marker tether (switch from id to frameioCommentId). Type-checked clean. Operational note: the file-based route move needs the running server to reload/rebuild to serve the new /comments path. Deliberately did NOT touch the *ByFrameioId store helpers or frameio service functions — those are still used by the webhook/mirror/shares paths.

title: Frame.io comment decoupling Step 4 — comment count computed on read (completes the decoupling)
summary: Final step: replaced the drift-prone denormalised asset.frameio.commentCount with a per-asset count computed on read via a single batched GROUP BY query (getCommentCountByAssetForProject), returned by the media-list route as commentCounts. MediaTab's new-comment toast now reads that ungated computed count (so non-Frame assets toast too) instead of the Frame.io-gated denormalised value. Removed all five denormalised write-paths (four in the comments route, one in the webhook) and trimmed the now-unused imports; the FrameIOInfo.commentCount field is marked deprecated. Notably there was never a rendered count badge — the count only fed the toast. This completes Steps 1-4: Frame.io is now optional for comments end to end (any asset commentable, comment_id is the stable identity, counts are computed). Type-checked clean. Remaining non-blocking cleanups: editpanel marker-tether switch to frameioCommentId, optional /frameio/comments route rename, optional removal of the deprecated field.

title: Frame.io comment decoupling Step 3 — stable comment identity (comment_id is the sole outward id)
summary: Retired the dual-identity model where a comment's outward id was frameio_comment_id ?? comment_id and flipped from local to Frame.io once the mirror landed. The outward id is now always the stable local comment_id; the Frame.io id is exposed as a separate frameioCommentId field for consumers that still tether on it (EditPanel markers). getThreadedCommentsForAssetVersion sets id=comment_id and emits frameioCommentId; the reply POST returns parentId=parent.commentId (permanently killing the reply-vanish race since the optimistic insert can no longer miss); the EP route filters on frameioCommentId != null; webhook + reply notifications reference the local comment_id. Internal frameio_comment_id is untouched (webhook idempotency, outbound mirror tether). Known deferred break: the editpanel client must switch its frameio:{id} marker tag from id to frameioCommentId. Type-checked clean. Step 4 (comment-count relocation) remains.

title: Frame.io comment decoupling Step 2 — comment UI now shows for non-Frame assets
summary: Removed the Frame.io render/handler gates so the comment UI works on assets that were never uploaded to Frame.io. In MediaDetailPanel: fetchComments and the load effects now key on asset.assetId (not frameio.assetId), the open effect always fetches versions, the sidebar compose handler dropped its Frame.io bail, and the Comments section render gate was removed. In MediaPlayer (theater): dropped frameioAssetId from the comment compose handler, the comments-icon render, and the timed-comment compose footer (the comments panel was already gated on panelContainer, not Frame.io). Pairs with Step 1's API change to make commenting on non-Frame assets work end to end. The real-time socket listener stays gated on Frame.io since those refresh events only come from Frame.io webhooks. Type-checked clean. The MediaTab grid count badge is still Frame.io-gated (Step 4). Steps 3-4 still to come.

title: Frame.io comment decoupling Step 1 — comments no longer require a Frame.io upload
summary: First step of making Frame.io optional for comments. The comments API route (frameio/comments) no longer hard-gates on asset.frameio.assetId: GET dropped its empty-list gate and POST dropped its 'not uploaded to Frame.io yet' 400. Added a shared resolveCommentScope helper that resolves the target asset_version from the Frame.io file-id mapping when present, else from the asset's current LPOS version via getCurrentAssetVersion. Outbound mirror enqueue is now conditional on the asset actually being on Frame.io, so LPOS-only assets keep their comments local instead of piling un-sendable jobs into the mirror queue. Existing Frame.io-backed assets behave exactly as before. Type-checked clean. Steps 2-4 (UI gate removal, stable comment identity, comment-count relocation) still to come.

title: Rename Domain Restrictions to Security and add signed URL toggle
summary: Renamed the Domain Restrictions button/modal to Security and added a Require Signed URLs checkbox. Wired requireSignedURLs through cloudflare-stream.ts, the cloudflare API route, and DomainRestrictionsModal so it reads and writes the CF Stream setting. Enables quick testing of whether the LeaderPass platform handles signed-URL-protected videos.

title: People prospect-stage "No stage" silently reverts — PATCH route's str() helper ignored null
summary: Fixed a bug where clearing the funnel Stage on a person (picking 'No stage') silently reverted to the previous stage. The inline ProspectStageBadge on the person detail page sends { prospectStage: value || null } when the option's empty value is selected, so the request body was { prospectStage: null }. The prospects PATCH route's str() coercion helper at app/api/prospects/[prospectId]/route.ts only handled string inputs — null fell through to its undefined branch, the field was dropped from the patch, the DB never updated, and the page re-rendered the stale value. Updated str() to treat null as an explicit clear (mirroring how the existing num() helper already behaved and how '' was already clearing), and switched the non-nullable status field check to a direct typeof body.status === 'string' test so the new null-clears semantic can't accidentally NULL out the status column. As a side effect this also fixes the same latent bug for the ~14 other str()-gated clearable fields (source, referredBy, accountModel, revenueType, expansionPotential, expectedStartMonth, owner, startMonth, recurringBillingStatus, renewalDate, firstRecurringBillDate, activeServices, nextFilmDate) that the in-tree edit-form save path also sends as field || null.

title: Asset move: keep historical activity events at the source
summary: Changed the asset-move behavior to leave historical activity_events at the SOURCE project (the rewrite-project_id step is dropped) and anchor only the asset.moved event at the TARGET. Future activity on the asset naturally lands at the target because the asset's project_id is now the target. Net effect: source project's activity feed retains the asset's pre-move story unchanged; target project's feed starts with the asset.moved event and accumulates new activity from there. Honest split — pre-move story belongs to the original home, post-move chapter belongs to the new one. Only the docstrings in app/api/projects/[projectId]/media/move/route.ts and lib/store/asset-move-store.ts were updated; the route was already writing the move event at the target so its code path needed no change. Helper drops the activity DB import + transaction block. Context for the decision: a thorough scan confirmed there's no per-project activity tab or per-asset activity panel in the UI today (only the global ActivityStrip and ActivityHistoryModal), so the asymmetry is not user-visible until/unless we build one — at which point the source side could grow an outbound counterpart event with one extra recordActivity call.

title: Follow-up tweaks: conditional Referred-by, prospect/client visual stripe, asset right-click move, + Tab modal, auto-Tab-1, tab delete confirm
summary: Six polish items on today's earlier batches. (1) Referred-by row/field now only renders when Source has a value — on the detail page it tracks the live source state mid-edit so the row appears/disappears as the user picks/clears Source. (2) Replaced the small 'Prospect'/'Client' text badge on people cards/rows with a left-edge color stripe (amber/green/muted) — leaves the corner badge free for the interesting info (stage chip on prospects, billing pill on active clients). Detail-page header drops the static 'Prospect' pill; the Promote → button already signals state. (3) Added 'Move to project…' to the asset right-click context menu in MediaTab with desktop-style semantics (act on multi-select when right-clicked asset is in the selection, else act on just the single asset). showMoveModal state widened from boolean to {assetIds: string[]} so both flows share the same modal. (4) Renamed '+ Day' to '+ Tab', replaced window.prompt with a custom inline modal (input + Cancel/Add, Enter submits), and moved the button out of the film-day pill bar into the sl-log-controls row right-justified next to Hide Log / Select / Export CSV. (5) On first tab creation in a project that already has notes, the server now auto-creates 'Tab 1' and bulk-assigns every untagged note to it BEFORE creating the user's named tab — preserves pre-tabs work in a clearly named container. Targeted slateTabCreatedAck event auto-activates the user's freshly named tab on the originating socket only. (6) Replaced the inline ✓/× tab-delete confirm with the shared ConfirmModal — danger-styled, body explains notes will move to Unassigned.

title: Move assets between projects (LPOS-only, bulk action from Internal Media)
summary: Added a 'Move to project…' bulk action to the Internal Media tab. Opens a new MoveAssetsModal with a grouped project picker (excludes source + archived projects), search, and a sticky banner warning that Frame.io references won't follow (LPOS-only move per spec). Confirm POSTs to a new /api/projects/[projectId]/media/move endpoint that runs a three-DB move helper: canonical-assets.sqlite rewrites assets.project_id; core.sqlite rewrites asset_share_links.project_id and detaches the asset from the old project's deliverable_assets; activity.sqlite rewrites the asset's historical events' project_id to the target so the new project's timeline shows the full asset history. Records one asset.moved activity event per successful move with from/to embedded in details_json as the canonical audit anchor. Child rows (asset_versions, media_files, distribution_records, editorial_links) follow implicitly via asset_id references. Per-asset failures returned individually so partial success keeps moving what it can. Frame.io references on the asset are intentionally untouched.

title: Film-day tabs on the Slate production notes panel
summary: Added a manual film-day tab system to /slate's Production Notes panel. Each project owns an independent list of SlateTab rows persisted in a new slate-tabs.json file (sibling to the existing slate-notes.json — no SQLite migration). The notes panel shows a horizontal pill bar above the note input: 'All' + each named tab + '+ Day' button. The active tab is clickable to switch, double-click to rename, with ◂/▸ reorder arrows, ✎ rename, and 🗑 → confirm/cancel delete inline buttons. Notes carry an optional tabId (added to the SlateNote interface) — when a specific tab is active the notes log filters to that day, and new notes auto-inherit the active tab id at addNote time. Old notes (no tabId) appear in 'All'. Tab delete re-homes affected notes back to Unassigned rather than destroying them (server clears tabId in memory + file, emits notesReloaded broadcast). New socket events on the SlateService: createSlateTab / renameSlateTab / reorderSlateTabs / deleteSlateTab / assignNoteToTab; addNote now accepts an optional tabId. Active tab persists per-project in localStorage so reopening a shoot re-lands on the same day. Schema is forward-compatible with the planned Google Sheets sync for production notes (one Sheets tab per slate tab).

title: NewTaskModal lazy-fetches preprod columns when opened outside DashboardClient
summary: Follow-up to the people-page task-icon commit. The inline UpdatesLog → NewTaskModal flow mounts the modal outside PreprodConfigProvider, so usePreprodConfig() returned the default empty context and the modal incorrectly tripped its 'no preprod columns yet' guard for prospects even when the Pre-Production board had columns. Added a lazy-fetch fallback: when taskType==='preprod' AND the context statuses are empty AND no lazy fetch has run yet, the modal calls GET /api/preprod-board/columns once and uses the result. Inside the provider (dashboard) the effect early-returns without hitting the API. No call-site changes; the modal handles its own fallback. Chose this over wrapping a higher layout in the provider to avoid fetching the column list on every navigation including unrelated pages.

title: People-page tweaks: Referred by, prospect stage badge, inline task creation
summary: Three people-page additions in one batch: (1) a free-text Referred by field under Source — appears in NewPersonModal and the Account panel on the detail page; autocompletes from existing People company names via <datalist>; saved as a new prospects.referred_by column (v22 migration); editable on both prospects and active clients. (2) A new prospect funnel badge with 7 free-select stages (Reached Out, Zoom Meeting Set, Post-Zoom Email Sent, Examples Sent, Proposal Sent, Blueprint SOW & Payment Link Sent, Contract Sent) — saved in a new prospects.prospect_stage column; shows alongside (not replacing) the existing Prospect status pill; rendered as a clickable pill-select in the detail header, a compact color-coded chip on list cards and rows, and a row in the Account panel; hidden on active/inactive clients per spec; PATCHes the prospect on every change. (3) A task icon button next to the existing attachment paperclip in the UpdatesLog compose footer — opens the dashboard's NewTaskModal pre-bound to this person (locked client + auto-fill); defaults to Pre-Production for prospects and shows a 3-button internal task-type picker for active clients (no forced default per user). NewTaskModal's taskType prop is now optional to support this 'no default' case; existing call sites unchanged.

title: Pre-Production task board (new /dashboard tab, admin-configurable columns)
summary: Added a third task_type ('preprod') alongside Editing/Platform on /dashboard, with a new task_phase_configs table backing fully admin-configurable columns instead of the hardcoded TASK_TYPE_CONFIGS used by the other two. The Pre-Production tab is the first entry in the toolbar tab list (preprod → editing → platform per user request); board is empty by default — no seed columns. Permission to add/rename/recolor/reorder/delete columns is a per-user access list (new preprod_board_admins table) mirroring the existing prospect-access / editpanel-access pattern; admins always pass. New API routes under /api/preprod-board/columns/ (GET open to any logged-in user; POST/PATCH/DELETE/reorder gated on the new requirePreprodBoardAdmin helper), and an admin-only /api/admin/preprod-board-admins for the access list. UI: new PreprodConfigContext provider wraps the dashboard so TaskBoard/TaskDetailModal/NewTaskModal all consume the live column list without prop-drilling; resolveTaskTypeConfig(taskType, dynamicPreprodStatuses?) merges DB-backed statuses for preprod and falls through to the static config for editing/platform. New PreprodColumnEditorModal opened from a 'Manage columns' toolbar button (permission-gated) gives add/rename (inline)/recolor (swatch-cycle through 13-color palette)/reorder (up/down arrows)/delete (with confirm + task-count guard surfaced from the API's 409 response — avoids silent task orphaning). Empty kanban shows a 'Set up columns' CTA for permitted users or polite copy for everyone else. Settings page gets a new PreprodBoardAccessPanel for admins to manage who can edit columns. Migration v21 adds the two new tables idempotently.

title: Delivery uploads heartbeat during multi-GB R2 transfers (no more 3-min false-fail)
summary: Delivery POST job auto-failed mid-upload because uploadToR2 ran for >3 min on multi-GB raw interview files (14–20 GB) while never emitting a setProgress call to refresh updatedAt — the queue's 3-min stale sweep killed the job even though bytes were actively streaming to R2. Fix: wire the AWS SDK Upload's httpUploadProgress event through uploadToR2 as an optional onProgress callback, then in the delivery route compute per-file progress bands (Phase A: 1..56 split N ways; Phase C: per-proxy band within 68..98) and emit setProgress on each tick with real bytes-uploaded text ('Uploading file 1 of 5: foo.mp4 — 2.3 GB / 16.9 GB'). Wrap transcodeProxy in a 60s queue.heartbeat interval since ffmpeg has no JS-side callbacks. Secondary fix: UploadQueueService.patch() now no-ops on terminal jobs, and fail/complete/cancel early-bail when already terminal — prevents a background IIFE that didn't notice the auto-fail from resurrecting the in-memory job state via late setProgress calls.

title: Comment reply date right-justified (parity with main comments)
summary: Comment replies in the asset sidebar rendered author and date as bare inline spans inside a non-flex parent, gluing them together (e.g. 'Jordan JohnsonJun 8, 2:53 PM'). Main comments don't have this problem because they wrap author/date in a .mad-comment-header flex container, which combines with the existing .mad-comment-date { margin-left: auto } rule to right-justify the date. Fix: wrap the reply's author + date spans in the same .mad-comment-header div the main comment uses. Zero new CSS — existing rules handle it once the parent becomes a flex container. Single JSX edit in components/media/MediaDetailPanel.tsx.

title: Version chip → hybrid semver (major.minor.<auto-patch>)
summary: Converted the top-left version chip from v.<commit-count> (e.g. v.78 · a1b2c3d) to a hybrid semver scheme <major>.<minor>.<patch> (e.g. 0.1.77 · a1b2c3d). major.minor come from package.json.version and are bumped manually when something user-noticeable ships; patch is auto-computed at server start as commits since the last commit that changed the "version": line in package.json. Bumping minor in package.json resets patch to 0 because the bump commit becomes the new anchor. Cannot forget to bump — patch always advances. lib/version.ts rewritten; major/minor/patch added to AppVersion; VersionTag component unchanged (only consumes display/sha/branch/date/dirty). docs/README.md Build / Version Tag section rewritten with the new scheme + bumping checklist. Runtime validated against the live repo before commit: 0.1.77* · 1a3dd50 (anchor at 0c62fea, 77 commits since, 0.1.0 in package.json).

title: Platform list column headers: larger + free-floating
summary: Tweaked the .platform-list-cols header row in the platform list view. Font-size bumped from 0.72rem to 0.85rem so the labels (Description, Client, Person, Status, Priority) read clearly as column headers. Removed the bar chrome that sat behind them: dropped background, border-bottom, position: sticky, top:0, and z-index:2. Headers now sit in normal document flow with no surface behind them — free-floating, uppercase + letter-spacing + 600 weight remain as the typographic cues that they're labels. Grid template, gap, casing, weight, and letter-spacing unchanged so alignment with row content stays pixel-identical.

title: Drag handles to reorder platform categories (any user)
summary: Added a per-category grip-icon drag handle on the left edge of every live category group in PlatformListView. Any signed-in (non-guest) user can grab a handle and drag the category up or down; the new order persists immediately via the existing POST /api/task-categories/reorder endpoint, whose auth gate dropped from admin to user (create/rename/delete remain admin-only). Task-into-category drag (the existing feature) keeps working unchanged — the two drag flows coexist in the same DndContext and are disambiguated by active.id prefix. DroppableCategoryGroup → SortableCategoryGroup using @dnd-kit/sortable (already a project dep). Only live categories are sortable; orphan/uncategorized groups stay pinned at the end and remain droppable for task drops. Optimistic reorder with rollback on POST failure. New CSS for the handle, the dragging visual, and the category drag-overlay ghost.

title: Transcript selection batch bar streams a zip (the actual one users use)
summary: Followup to the earlier transcripts-zip fix. The 'Download all transcripts' button (server-side `download-all` route) was already correct — verified end-to-end via curl against the running server, returns a valid 95-file zip. But the path users actually use — the in-list selection batch bar in components/projects/ProjectDetail.tsx (Download TXT / Download Timecoded buttons that appear when transcripts are checkbox-selected) — was untouched and still triggered N individual <a>.click() events with 300ms gaps between each. Symptom: select 3, get 3 separate files. Fixed by adding POST /api/projects/[projectId]/transcripts/download-zip (selection-driven, accepts {jobIds, type}) and rewriting batchDownload to POST + save the response blob. Single-file fast path preserved on both server and client per the original 'no zip when only one' rule. Same archiver+PassThrough+Readable.toWeb pattern as the existing download-all and photos/download-zip routes.

title: Decision: defer comment-recency cache; plan full Frame.io-comment decoupling
summary: Confirmed via SQL probe that activity_events has zero frameio.comment.* rows in production — Frame.io webhooks aren't producing local data, which is why the MediaTab 'Latest comments' sort falls through to alphabetical for every pair. A small recency-cache fix was proposed (new asset_comment_recency table + three writers + reader rewrite, ~80 LOC). User chose to defer the small fix and queue the larger refactor: full local comments table in LPOS with bidirectional Frame.io sync during a transition period, then Frame.io becomes optional. Sort fix lands 'for free' once the local comments table exists. Backfill strategy chosen for the future refactor: lazy only — no eager admin backfill, no boot-time backfill. No code changed in this entry; the refactor plan is recorded in project history and in a memory note for future sessions.

title: Breadcrumb/home occlusion guard
summary: Forward-looking guard so the top-left breadcrumb (back arrow + home icon) cannot be hidden by a future modal or overlay. Bumped .breadcrumb-bar z-index from 40 to 10500, above the highest currently-used overlay layer (10000). Added a translucent dark backdrop with backdrop-filter: blur(6px) so the icons stay legible when floating over a modal backdrop. Added a drop-in .breadcrumb-bar--locked modifier (dim + non-interactive) as the preferred opt-out for flows that legitimately need to block navigation. Recorded the invariant and an 'adding a new overlay' checklist in docs/README.md.

title: Audit: "Sort by latest comment" in project media
summary: Read-through audit of the sort-by-latest-comment path in MediaTab — the DB query, API serialization, webhook ingest, and UI comparator. Core mechanism is correct (indexes are right, asset_id is always set, Map→Record doesn't drop entries, comparator nulls-last is intentional). Three behavioral issues were surfaced for user decision and NOT fixed in this entry: (1) LPOS-authored comments don't update the sort until the Frame.io webhook echoes back — a webhook delay or drop leaves the sort stale; (2) comment edits/completions/deletions don't bump recency because the webhook handler drops everything except comment.created — this is a design call about what 'latest' means; (3) webhook drops events when the asset's frameio.assetId no longer matches. Audit-only entry — no code changed.

title: Bulk transcript download streams a zip
summary: Rewrote /api/projects/[projectId]/transcripts/download-all from a concatenated plaintext blob to a streamed .zip, one .txt per transcript named by display filename, with collision-safe deduping. Same archiver+PassThrough pattern as photos/download-zip. Preserves a single-transcript fast path: when only one transcript exists, the route streams the single .txt directly with no zip wrapper, per the user's stated rule. Cross-browser/OS safe via standard application/zip + Content-Disposition headers; the existing 'Download all transcripts' button needs no change.

title: Copy-link button shows checkmark + "Link copied"
summary: Added in-button visual feedback to the 'Copy link to this asset' button in MediaDetailPanel's sidebar header. On a successful clipboard write the chain icon swaps to a checkmark, a green-tinted 'Link copied' label appears next to it, aria-label/title flip to 'Link copied', and the state resets after 1.8s. Mirrors the per-review-link copy pattern already used elsewhere in the same component. The existing success toast is kept as a redundant signal; the in-button affordance is now the primary cue.

title: Decouple attachment serving from Prospects access
summary: Fixed a bug where users without Prospects access couldn't open attachments on ordinary tasks. The shared attachment download endpoint (/api/attachment) serves both task-comment and prospect-update attachments but unconditionally required Prospects access, returning a 403 for everyone else. It now authorizes by the attachment's key prefix: task attachments (attachments/tasks/<id>/…) require only a valid session, matching how task-comment uploads are gated, while prospect attachments (attachments/<prospectId>/…) still require Prospects access. Keys are minted server-side so the prefix is a trusted discriminator; the R2 storage service, upload routes, data model, and frontend were already domain-correct and unchanged.

title: Notify original commenter when their comment gets a reply
summary: Added a new persistent notification category for media-comment replies, mirroring the existing Task/Prospect/Delivery notification slices. When a reply lands on a comment that was authored inside LPOS, the original commenter now gets a bell notification under a new 'Comments' tab — persisted in a comment_notifications table, pushed live via Socket.io ('comment:notification') plus best-effort web-push, and deep-linking to /projects/{id}?assetId={asset}. New model/store/service/hook/API routes were added and the reply POST handler resolves the parent author from comment-authors-store, firing only when an LPOS userId exists (external Frame.io reviewers have no in-app recipient) and skipping self-replies. The notif panel was widened to fit a 5th tab without clipping. Reply mechanism itself is unchanged.

title: Right-align comment "Reply" button
summary: Right-aligned the per-comment Reply trigger in both the media detail panel (.mad-reply-btn) and theater mode (.vt-cp-reply-btn) by giving each a fit-content block with margin-left:auto, so it sits at the right edge under each comment instead of bottom-left. CSS-only; the in-compose Reply/Cancel rows were already right-aligned. Reply mechanism unchanged: Frame.io has no reply endpoint, so LPOS posts a 'Reply to above:' top-level comment and reconstructs threads from a local replyId→parentId map.

title: Fix: checked-off Frame.io comment resets moments later
summary: Fixed a race where marking a Frame.io comment complete would optimistically check, then un-check itself moments later. The completed flag lives only in Frame.io; the user's PATCH triggers Frame.io's comment.completed webhook, which relays back as a comment-list refresh, but Frame.io's read API briefly lags its own webhook so the refetch returns the stale pre-toggle value. The optimistic guard (pendingTogglesRef) was cleared the instant the PATCH resolved — right before the echo landed — so it no longer masked the stale read; theater-mode toggles never set the guard at all. Now the optimistic value is sticky until a refetch confirms Frame.io has caught up (guard cleared only when a fetched comment's completed matches the pending value), the toggle handler keeps the guard on success, and theater-mode toggles register the guard too.

title: Move version chip from top-right to top-left
summary: Relocated the build version chip from `right: 8px` to `left: 8px` in `.version-tag` so it no longer competes visually with the notif-bell, user-menu, and storage-gear cluster on the right. Top-left at `top: 4px` sits above the breadcrumb bar (which starts at `top: 20px left: 32px`) and clear of the centered navbar pill — the only fully open corner of the shell.

title: Auto-advancing build version chip in top-right corner
summary: Added a tiny fixed-position chip in the top-right corner showing `v.<commit-count> · <short-sha>`. The commit count auto-advances on every git commit (and therefore every push); clicking the chip copies the full SHA so we can `git checkout` to the exact build a user reported a bug against — directly addressing the recent need to recover lost code. Implementation reads git via `execSync` once at server start in `lib/version.ts`, caches the result, passes it from the server `layout.tsx` to `AppShell` as a prop, and renders via `components/shell/VersionTag.tsx`. A `*` suffix appears when the running tree had uncommitted changes at boot.

title: Mobile layout audit and responsive fixes
summary: Audited every page group for elements overflowing on phone screens and appended a consolidated mobile-only CSS block to globals.css. Home tiles now wrap instead of clipping off-screen; the project workflow nav became a horizontal-scroll pill strip instead of 7 oversized stacked buttons; the client grid collapses 4 to 2 to 1 columns; slide-in side panels (shares, script editor) lift above the bottom tab bar; and several toolbars and media rows stop forcing horizontal overflow. All changes are gated behind max-width media queries, so the desktop layout is unchanged.

title: Add "All" scope tab to task board
summary: Added a third scope tab (All) to the Mine / Others toggle on the task board. Selecting All shows every task of the active type regardless of assignment. Required only a type union update and a new button — the existing filter already had a passthrough return true for unknown scopes.

title: HLS playback via hls.js
summary: Switched all video players from raw Frame.io originalUrl (raw uploaded file) to highQualityUrl (H.264 HLS transcode). Added useHlsPlayer hook that uses native HLS on Safari and hls.js on Chrome/Firefox/Edge. Fixes .mov playback cross-browser and improves scrubbing performance via adaptive bitrate streaming. Falls back to originalUrl if transcode not ready.

title: Git push to remote
summary: Staged and pushed 111 changed/new files from lpos-dashboard to github.com/lp-jordan/lpos main branch (commit 6584493). Excluded .DS_Store and atem-bridge.zip. Covers all accumulated changes since the 4-17-26 commit.

title: Sardius filename collision handling
summary: Added filename conflict detection to the Sardius push flow. The POST API now calls checkSardiusFileExists before starting an upload and returns HTTP 409 with a suggestedName ('filename(1).mp4') if the file already exists and the caller has not acknowledged. The SardiusPushModal handles the 409 by pausing the upload loop and presenting Overwrite / Rename options inline; for batch pushes, each conflicting asset is resolved in sequence before the loop continues.

title: Sardius FTP push feature
summary: Added a Sardius media push workflow accessible from the media asset More Info sidebar. A modal connects to the Akamai FTP watch-folder server, lists the remote directory tree, and lets the user pick a destination, set per-asset metadata (speakers, categories, publish profile), preview the JSON sidecar, and trigger a background FTP upload. After Sardius processes the file, the user pastes the assigned share URL back into LPOS where it is stored and available to copy with one click. Status cycles: none → uploading → queued → ready.
